name: Sentinel Oak
body:
Sentinel Oak
CR 21

This enormous oak is unspeakably majestic, even despite its gnarled appearance, grotesquely thick trunk and leafless branches. You can feel its power in your bones as you look at it, and its mighty presence seems to invade your mind.

XP 409,600
NG Colossal plant (extraplanar)
Init –1; Senses blindsight 300 ft., detect thoughts, greater arcane sight, tremorsense 200 ft., true seeing; Perception +39; Aura unreality (10 miles)

DEFENSE

AC 37, touch 7, flat-footed 37 (+10 deflection, –5 Dex, +30 natural, –8 size)
hp 435 (30d8+300); regeneration 10 (deific or mythic)
Fort +27, Ref +7, Will +19
Defensive Abilities psychic deflection, roots; DR 10/epic; Immune ability damage, ability drain, petrification, plant traits, sonic; Resist acid 30, cold 30, electricity 30, fire 30; SR 32

OFFENSE

Speed 0 ft. (immobile)
Melee 4 slams +27 (6d6+12/19-20 plus awesome blow)
Space 30 ft.; Reach 30 ft.
Special Attacks detect thoughts
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 30th; concentration +40)

Constant—detect thoughts (DC 22), greater arcane sight, true seeing
At will—animate objects, animate plants, call lightning storm (DC 25), control plants, dispel magic, entangle (DC 21), fear (DC 24), imprisonment (DC 30), lightning bolt (DC 23), telekinesis (DC 25), wall of thorns
3/day—baleful polymorph (DC 25), break enchantment, chain lightning (DC 26), insanity (DC 27), limited wish, mind thrust VI (DC 26), waves of exhaustion
1/day—dominate monster (DC 29), earthquake, mass charm monster (DC 28), summon nature’s ally IX
1/year—wish

STATISTICS

Str 35, Dex 1, Con 31, Int 24, Wis 28, Cha 30
Base Atk +22; CMB +42; CMD 65 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Combat Expertise, Critical Focus, Defensive Combat Training, Greater Spell Penetration, Improved Critical (slam), Improved Initiative, Improved Lightning Reflexes, Improved Vital Strike, Lightning Reflexes, Power Attack, Spell Focus (abjuration), Spell Penetration, Staggering Critical, Stunning Critical, Weapon Focus (slam)
Skills Bluff +30, Diplomacy +30, Intimidate +30, Knowledge (arcana, history, nature, planes, religion) +37, Perception +39, Sense Motive +39
Languages Aklo, Common, Druidic, Sylvan (can’t speak); telepathy 300 ft.
SQ eternal watch

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Aura of Unreality (Su)

A sentinel oak warps the terrain around it with its eldritch dominance. Its effects, and the extent of the sentinel oak’s control, differ with range.

10 miles: Within this range, a sentinel oak can freely manipulate weather, as if by the control weather spell.
1 mile: The terrain seems to shift and warp, along with the sounds and colors. Affected creatures treat all terrain within as difficult and are sickened unless they succeed at a DC 35 Will save. A sentinel oak may exclude creatures from this effect.
500 feet: A sentinel oak may affect any area within this radius with an effect that mimics spellscar or storm of vengeance spells as a swift action. A sentinel oak is immune to these effects.
Awesome Blow (Ex)

A sentinel oak can swat opponents away with its powerful branches. After hitting a creature with its slam attack, a sentinel oak may attempt a combat maneuver against this creature. If it succeeds, the creature is sent flying, as per the awesome blow feat.

Eternal Watch (Su)

A creature under the effect of the sentinel oak’s imprisonment spell-like ability cannot be freed even with a freedom spell or if brought into the confines of an antimagic field unless the freeing effect’s creator succeeds at a DC 41 caster level check.

Psychic Deflection (Su)

A sentinel oak adds its Charisma modifier as a deflection bonus to its AC.

Roots (Ex)

A sentinel oak is immune to any non-magical effects that would move it in any way, such as bull rush attempts. Moving a sentinel oak with a magical effect requires the caster to succeed at a DC 41 caster level check. The sentinel oak’s massive root system makes it difficult to kill. After it sustains fatal damage, the sentinel oak begins to regenerate and can grow back to its previous size in 1d4 weeks. Dealing 50 points of mythic fire damage to the sentinel oak’s root system after it has sustained fatal damage prevents this regeneration.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

The first sentinel oaks were summoned in ancient times from a primordial plane, though which one it was exactly was lost to the passage of time. What is clear is their purpose, which is to guard sites where ancient evils were buried by forces either unwilling or unable to destroy them for good. With an ability to entomb creatures beneath their roots so thoroughly that only deific power could extract them, these powerful trees are unbreakable sentries and unflinching jailors all in one. A sentinel oak, while immobile, holds enormous power which it can exert over its surroundings and any creatures that enter its domain. From weather manipulation, through animating its surroundings, to psychic onslaughts and even wishcraft, their capabilities often equal or surpass those of the very evils they guard.

Sentinel oaks are exceedingly rare, and are among very few creatures that hold power over an arsenal of magic that seemingly blends the arcane, divine and even psychic powers. A sentinel oak is never without a prisoner, and most of them guard powerful outsiders or undead that would rejuvenate if destroyed. Reportedly, some worlds hold sentinel oaks of mythic power that guard prisons of thoroughly evil demigods, including some demon lords long thought dead or lost.

Most sentinel oaks remain ever vigilant, intolerant of any intrusion into their domain, fearing their lenience may lead to unforeseen consequences. These often live on desolate wastelands of their own creation, either scaring off any intruders, enslaving them with powerful magic and recruiting them to help garrison the eternal prison, or outright destroying them if they so much as suspect their evil intent. Other sentinel oaks are eager, though slow, conversationalists, fond of passing their uneventful lives chatting with guests and assisting them with minor issues.

While knowledge of rituals needed to summon a sentinel oak is lost to time, the trees themselves hold an ability to procreate. A sentinel oak may create an offspring, which is called a sapling, using its yearly wish ability. That sapling manifests within the reach of its parent’s branches as a separate creature. Sentinel oaks create saplings extremely rarely, and only when they are convinced of a new evil that has to be guarded in its prison elsewhere. What follows is a brief instruction to its child, and subsequent permission for the pleading creatures to carry and escort it to its post.

A fully grown sentinel oak averages 80 feet in height, with a trunk almost half as thick in circumference. Truly powerful and ancient individuals may be larger, while freshly spawned saplings barely exceed 8 feet in height. Sentinel oaks can theoretically die of old age, though their lifespans are measured in millions of years, meaning they are virtually immortal to most beings.

A sapling of a sentinel oak starts off only Large and with 9 Hit Dice, lacking most powers of its ancestor. It grows quickly, gaining 3 HD each year, becoming Huge at 12 HD, Gargantuan at 21 HD and finally Colossal at 30 HD, gaining more and more power as it grows. While it differs from sapling to sapling, a good rule of thumb is to give it only spell-like abilities with a spell level no higher than a third of its HD, scaling the existing ones down when appropriate (such as by giving it lower levels of mind thrust and summon nature’s ally). A sapling always has its imprisonment spell-like ability, regardless of HD and size category, but it has to be at least gargantuan to create a solid root system, and can be physically moved up to this point.
